review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

12:1.sourceText: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα ἦλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν, ὅπου ἦν Λάζαρος, ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν Ἰησοῦς.
12:1.targetText: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.

groups.note: ὅπου ἦν ("where … was") is rendered the hometown of.
BSB renders the repeated name Ἰησοῦς as He.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.

12:2.sourceText: ἐποίησαν οὖν αὐτῷ δεῖπνον ἐκεῖ, καὶ ἡ Μάρθα διηκόνει, ὁ δὲ Λάζαρος εἷς ἦν ἐκ τῶν ἀνακειμένων σὺν αὐτῷ·
12:2.targetText: So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Him.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτῷ ("for him").
εἷς … ἐκ ("one of") is rendered among.
The article with the participle ἀνακειμένων is rendered those reclining at the table.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:3.sourceText: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ λαβοῦσα λίτραν μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτίμου ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἐξέμαξεν ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ· ἡ δὲ οἰκία ἐπληρώθη ἐκ τῆς ὀσμῆς τοῦ μύρου.
12:3.targetText: Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.

groups.note: λίτρα is a Roman pound, about twelve ounces.
The genitive νάρδου ("of nard") is rendered made of nard.
πόδας ("feet") is rendered them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτοῦ ("his") unexpressed after them.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle λαβοῦσα is rendered as the finite verb took.

12:4.sourceText: λέγει δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, ὁ μέλλων αὐτὸν παραδιδόναι
12:4.targetText: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him, asked,

groups.note: BSB's Greek has an extra word here with the same meaning; in N1904 the genitive alone gives "of".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:5.sourceText: Διὰ τί τοῦτο τὸ μύρον οὐκ ἐπράθη τριακοσίων δηναρίων καὶ ἐδόθη πτωχοῖς;
12:5.targetText: “Why wasn’t this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?”

groups.note: Διὰ τί ("because of what") is rendered Why.
The contraction wasn’t holds both the negative οὐκ and the passive auxiliary of ἐπράθη.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject of given; the Greek says only "and be given to the poor".

12:6.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ τοῦτο οὐχ ὅτι περὶ τῶν πτωχῶν ἔμελεν αὐτῷ, ἀλλ’ ὅτι κλέπτης ἦν καὶ τὸ γλωσσόκομον ἔχων τὰ βαλλόμενα ἐβάσταζεν.
12:6.targetText: Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. As keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it.

groups.note: BSB places the negative of οὐχ ὅτι ("not because") with the verb.
The participle ἔχων ("having") is rendered As keeper of.
The article with the participle βαλλόμενα is rendered what was put.
The imperfect ἐβάσταζεν ("he was carrying off") is rendered used to take from.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.
English makes explicit where the money was put.

12:7.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἄφες αὐτήν, ἵνα εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ ἐνταφιασμοῦ μου τηρήσῃ αὐτό·
12:7.targetText: “Leave her alone,” Jesus replied. “She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial.

groups.note: ἀφίημι means "let go", "leave alone".
εἰς ("for, with a view to") is rendered in preparation for.
αὐτό ("it") is rendered this perfume.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns the ἵνα clause ("so that she may keep it") into a statement.

12:8.sourceText: τοὺς πτωχοὺς γὰρ πάντοτε ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε.
12:8.targetText: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.”

groups.note: The present ἔχετε ("you have") is rendered with will.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ (for) untranslated.

12:9.sourceText: Ἔγνω οὖν ὁ ὄχλος πολὺς ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὅτι ἐκεῖ ἐστιν, καὶ ἦλθον οὐ διὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον, ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἴδωσιν ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
12:9.targetText: Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there. And they came not only because of Him, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.

groups.note: BSB renders the name Ἰησοῦν as Him, since Jesus is named just before.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

12:10.sourceText: ἐβουλεύσαντο δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἀποκτείνωσιν,
12:10.targetText: So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:11.sourceText: ὅτι πολλοὶ δι’ αὐτὸν ὑπῆγον τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἐπίστευον εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
12:11.targetText: for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus.

groups.note: ὑπῆγον ("were going away") is rendered were deserting.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for deserting; the Greek has none.

12:12.sourceText: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος πολὺς ὁ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἔρχεται Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα,
12:12.targetText: The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐλθών is rendered that had come.

12:13.sourceText: ἔλαβον τὰ βαΐα τῶν φοινίκων καὶ ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐκραύγαζον Ὡσαννά, εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, καὶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
12:13.targetText: They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting:  “Hosanna!”   “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”   “Blessed is the King of Israel!”

groups.note: εὐλογημένος is understood again with the King of Israel, and BSB repeats it.
With the indeclinable name Ἰσραήλ, the article shows the genitive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns καὶ ἐκραύγαζον ("and they were shouting") into the participle shouting.
The καί ("even") is not expressed; BSB makes the King of Israel a second acclamation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has the participle εὐλογημένος alone.
English supplies the copula with the repeated Blessed.

12:14.sourceText: εὑρὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὀνάριον ἐκάθισεν ἐπ’ αὐτό, καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον
12:14.targetText: Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written:

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:15.sourceText: Μὴ φοβοῦ, θυγάτηρ Σιών· ἰδοὺ ὁ Βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται, καθήμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου.
12:15.targetText: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:16.sourceText: Ταῦτα οὐκ ἔγνωσαν αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ τὸ πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ ὅτε ἐδοξάσθη Ἰησοῦς τότε ἐμνήσθησαν ὅτι ταῦτα ἦν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα καὶ ταῦτα ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ.
12:16.targetText: At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.

groups.note: τὸ πρῶτον ("the first") is an adverbial phrase.
BSB reverses the two facts; καί joins "written about him" and "done to him".
The active ἐποίησαν ("they did") is rendered as a passive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves τότε ("then") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a second verb; in the Greek both facts depend on remembered.
English adds very for emphasis.

12:17.sourceText: Ἐμαρτύρει οὖν ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ὢν μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὅτε τὸν Λάζαρον ἐφώνησεν ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου καὶ ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
12:17.targetText: Meanwhile, many people continued to testify that they had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.

groups.note: The imperfect Ἐμαρτύρει ("was testifying") is rendered continued to testify.
The article with the participle ("the crowd that was with him") is rendered as what they testified.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces what they testified; the Greek has no conjunction.

12:18.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος, ὅτι ἤκουσαν τοῦτο αὐτὸν πεποιηκέναι τὸ σημεῖον.
12:18.targetText: That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered That is why.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula.
English introduces the reported fact; the Greek has an accusative with infinitive.

12:19.sourceText: οἱ οὖν Φαρισαῖοι εἶπαν πρὸς ἑαυτούς Θεωρεῖτε ὅτι οὐκ ὠφελεῖτε οὐδέν· ἴδε ὁ κόσμος ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθεν.
12:19.targetText: Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!”

groups.note: οὐκ … οὐδέν ("not … nothing") is rendered no.
ὠφελεῖτε ("you are gaining") is rendered is doing you … good.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject; in the Greek "you" are the ones who gain nothing.
English exclamation after Look.
English intensifier; the Greek says "the world".

12:20.sourceText: Ἦσαν δὲ Ἕλληνές τινες ἐκ τῶν ἀναβαινόντων ἵνα προσκυνήσωσιν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ·
12:20.targetText: Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀναβαινόντων is rendered those who went up.

12:21.sourceText: οὗτοι οὖν προσῆλθον Φιλίππῳ τῷ ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες Κύριε, θέλομεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδεῖν.
12:21.targetText: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and requested of him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”

groups.note: The article τῷ ("the one") is rendered who.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγοντες (saying) is represented only by the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula.

12:22.sourceText: ἔρχεται ὁ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἀνδρέᾳ· ἔρχεται Ἀνδρέας καὶ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγουσιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
12:22.targetText: Philip relayed this appeal to Andrew, and both of them went and told Jesus.

groups.note: ἔρχεται … καὶ λέγει ("comes and tells") is condensed to relayed.
Ἀνδρέας καὶ Φίλιππος ("Andrew and Philip") is rendered both of them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for relayed.
English joins the two sentences; the Greek has no connective here.

12:23.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀποκρίνεται αὐτοῖς λέγων Ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
12:23.targetText: But Jesus replied, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

groups.note: ἀποκρίνεται … λέγων ("answers … saying") is condensed to replied.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed after replied.

12:24.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ ὁ κόκκος τοῦ σίτου πεσὼν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἀποθάνῃ, αὐτὸς μόνος μένει· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ, πολὺν καρπὸν φέρει.
12:24.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.

groups.note: μόνος ("alone") is rendered only.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle πεσών is rendered as the finite verb falls.
English supplies a noun after only; the Greek says "it remains alone".

12:25.sourceText: ὁ φιλῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολλύει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ μισῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον φυλάξει αὐτήν.
12:25.targetText: Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.

groups.note: The present ἀπολλύει ("loses") is rendered with will.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:26.sourceText: ἐὰν ἐμοί τις διακονῇ, ἐμοὶ ἀκολουθείτω, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ, ἐκεῖ καὶ ὁ διάκονος ὁ ἐμὸς ἔσται· ἐάν τις ἐμοὶ διακονῇ, τιμήσει αὐτὸν ὁ Πατήρ.
12:26.targetText: If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.

groups.note: The article with the possessive ἐμός ("the my") is rendered My.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἐκεῖ ("there") untranslated after where I am.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:27.sourceText: νῦν ἡ ψυχή μου τετάρακται, καὶ τί εἴπω; Πάτερ, σῶσόν με ἐκ τῆς ὥρας ταύτης. ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ὥραν ταύτην.
12:27.targetText: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.

groups.note: ἀλλά ("but") is rendered No, rejecting the prayer just voiced.
διά with τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered for this purpose.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft construction; the Greek has none.
English cleft construction; the Greek has none.

12:28.sourceText: Πάτερ, δόξασόν σου τὸ ὄνομα. ἦλθεν οὖν φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ Καὶ ἐδόξασα καὶ πάλιν δοξάσω.
12:28.targetText: Father, glorify Your name!”  Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The first καί ("both") is not expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; the Greek has none.
English supplies an object; the Greek has none.

12:29.sourceText: ὁ οὖν ὄχλος ὁ ἑστὼς καὶ ἀκούσας ἔλεγεν βροντὴν γεγονέναι· ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Ἄγγελος αὐτῷ λελάληκεν.
12:29.targetText: The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said that an angel had spoken to Him.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἑστώς is rendered standing there.
καί joins the two participles; BSB makes heard and said the two verbs.
βροντὴν γεγονέναι ("thunder had occurred") is rendered it had thundered.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for heard; the Greek has none.
English introduces the reported statement; the Greek has an accusative with infinitive.
English turns the direct quotation into reported speech.

12:30.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Οὐ δι’ ἐμὲ ἡ φωνὴ αὕτη γέγονεν ἀλλὰ δι’ ὑμᾶς.
12:30.targetText: In response, Jesus said, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.

groups.note: δι’ ἐμέ ("for my sake") is rendered for My benefit.
γέγονεν ("has come") is rendered was.
δι’ ὑμᾶς ("for your sake") is rendered yours, short for for your benefit.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί is not expressed; BSB renders ἀπεκρίθη as In response.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:31.sourceText: νῦν κρίσις ἐστὶν τοῦ κόσμου τούτου· νῦν ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἐκβληθήσεται ἔξω·
12:31.targetText: Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.

groups.note: The genitive τοῦ κόσμου ("of the world") is rendered upon the world.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:32.sourceText: κἀγὼ ἐὰν ὑψωθῶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς, πάντας ἑλκύσω πρὸς ἐμαυτόν.
12:32.targetText: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.”

12:33.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ ἤμελλεν ἀποθνήσκειν.
12:33.targetText: He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

12:34.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ πῶς λέγεις σὺ ὅτι δεῖ ὑψωθῆναι τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου; τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
12:34.targetText: The crowd replied, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. So how can You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”

groups.note: The present μένει ("remains") is rendered will remain.
εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("into the age") is rendered forever.
λέγεις ("do you say") is rendered can … say.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed after replied.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:35.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔτι μικρὸν χρόνον τὸ φῶς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν. περιπατεῖτε ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε, ἵνα μὴ σκοτία ὑμᾶς καταλάβῃ· καὶ ὁ περιπατῶν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ οὐκ οἶδεν ποῦ ὑπάγει.
12:35.targetText: Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.

groups.note: Ἔτι ("still") is rendered longer.
μικρὸν χρόνον ("a little time") is rendered for a little while.
The present ἐστιν ("is") is rendered will be.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves the connective καί untranslated.

12:36.sourceText: ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε, πιστεύετε εἰς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα υἱοὶ φωτὸς γένησθε. Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἐκρύβη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
12:36.targetText: While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.”  After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them.

groups.note: BSB turns the two καί-joined clauses into an After-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀπελθών is rendered as the finite verb went away.

12:37.sourceText: Τοσαῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ σημεῖα πεποιηκότος ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν,
12:37.targetText: Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("he").
The genitive absolute participle πεποιηκότος supplies the Although-clause.
ἔμπροσθεν ("before") is rendered in … presence.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English stresses the contrast with Although.

12:38.sourceText: ἵνα ὁ λόγος Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου πληρωθῇ ὃν εἶπεν Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων Κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη;
12:38.targetText: This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet:  “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

groups.note: The passive πληρωθῇ ("might be fulfilled") is rendered as the active fulfill.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB represents ὃν εἶπεν ("which he spoke") only by the colon before the quotation.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a main clause; the Greek continues the sentence with ἵνα.

12:39.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἠδύναντο πιστεύειν, ὅτι πάλιν εἶπεν Ἡσαΐας
12:39.targetText: For this reason they were unable to believe. For again, Isaiah says:

groups.note: διά ("because of") with τοῦτο is rendered for this reason.
οὐκ ἠδύναντο ("they could not") is rendered they were unable.

12:40.sourceText: Τετύφλωκεν αὐτῶν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ ἐπώρωσεν αὐτῶν τὴν καρδίαν, ἵνα μὴ ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ νοήσωσιν τῇ καρδίᾳ καὶ στραφῶσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
12:40.targetText: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.”

groups.note: μὴ ἴδωσιν ("may not see") is rendered cannot see; the contraction holds both the negative and the modal of the subjunctive.
The article τοῖς is rendered as the possessive their.
The article τῇ is rendered as the possessive their.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:41.sourceText: ταῦτα εἶπεν Ἡσαΐας ὅτι εἶδεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλησεν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
12:41.targetText: Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about Him.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:42.sourceText: ὅμως μέντοι καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχόντων πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς Φαρισαίους οὐχ ὡμολόγουν, ἵνα μὴ ἀποσυνάγωγοι γένωνται·
12:42.targetText: Nevertheless, many of the leaders believed in Him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.

groups.note: ὅμως μέντοι ("yet nevertheless") is rendered Nevertheless.
ἵνα μή ("so that not") is rendered for fear that.
ἀποσυνάγωγοι is one Greek adjective, "expelled from the synagogue".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("even") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for confess; the Greek has none.

12:43.sourceText: ἠγάπησαν γὰρ τὴν δόξαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων μᾶλλον ἤπερ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
12:43.targetText: For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:44.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἔκραξεν καὶ εἶπεν Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ πιστεύει εἰς ἐμὲ ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸν πέμψαντά με,
12:44.targetText: Then Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.

groups.note: ἔκραξεν καὶ εἶπεν ("cried out and said") is condensed to cried out.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds alone to make the contrast clear.

12:45.sourceText: καὶ ὁ θεωρῶν ἐμὲ θεωρεῖ τὸν πέμψαντά με.
12:45.targetText: And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.

12:46.sourceText: ἐγὼ φῶς εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐλήλυθα, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ μὴ μείνῃ.
12:46.targetText: I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.

groups.note: φῶς ("light") stands in apposition to I.
πᾶς … μή ("everyone … not") is rendered no one.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:47.sourceText: καὶ ἐάν τίς μου ἀκούσῃ τῶν ῥημάτων καὶ μὴ φυλάξῃ, ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω αὐτόν· οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον ἵνα κρίνω τὸν κόσμον, ἀλλ’ ἵνα σώσω τὸν κόσμον.
12:47.targetText: As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.

groups.note: ἐάν τις ("if anyone") is rendered As for anyone who.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for keep; the Greek has none.

12:48.sourceText: ὁ ἀθετῶν ἐμὲ καὶ μὴ λαμβάνων τὰ ῥήματά μου ἔχει τὸν κρίνοντα αὐτόν· ὁ λόγος ὃν ἐλάλησα, ἐκεῖνος κρινεῖ αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ·
12:48.targetText: There is a judge for the one who rejects Me and does not receive My words: The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.

groups.note: ἔχει ("has") is rendered There is … for.
The article with the participle κρίνοντα ("the one judging") is rendered a judge.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not repeat αὐτόν ("him"); it refers back to the one who rejects.
BSB leaves the resumptive ἐκεῖνος ("that one"), which repeats the word, untranslated.

12:49.sourceText: ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλάλησα, ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με Πατὴρ αὐτός μοι ἐντολὴν δέδωκεν τί εἴπω καὶ τί λαλήσω.
12:49.targetText: I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.

groups.note: ἐντολὴν δέδωκεν ("has given a command") is rendered has commanded.
τί ("what") is rendered how.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὅτι ("for") untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτός ("himself") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for say; the Greek has none.

12:50.sourceText: καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιός ἐστιν. ἃ οὖν ἐγὼ λαλῶ, καθὼς εἴρηκέν μοι ὁ Πατήρ, οὕτως λαλῶ.
12:50.targetText: And I know that His command leads to eternal life. So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.”

groups.note: ἐστιν ("is") is rendered leads to.
καθὼς … οὕτως ("just as … so") is rendered exactly.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
